d: With his days winding down, an aging gunman sets out on a quest to perform one last good deed, hoping to save his soul.
Author James P. Muehlberger talks about the 1869 killing of a bank cashier in Missouri; this has been considered the first in a long line of robberies by Jesse and Frank James.
Pete Grant controls the town of Pecos and it's Mayor and Marshal. When Jimmy, Denny, and Lasses arrive they soon find themselves in trouble.
Jewel-robbing bandits become the quarry of two United States marshals.
Rod Drew (John Wayne) is asked to search for missing people in Canada, and quickly finds out a gang of French Canadian outlaws have been kidnapping people.
Ted and Dusty infiltrate a band of outlaws to get close to Mr. Gentry, the man who murdered Ted's father.
A member of a powerful gang murders a shopkeeper; the deputized Cartwrights sentence a murderer to hang at dawn when the leader of the gang kidnaps Ben and holds him hostage.
A young bank robber gets a job on the Ponderosa to prevent the sheriff from finding the other members of his gang.
A banker, a judge and a rancher had motive to kill a newlywed editor.
Range Rider (Jock Mahoney) and Dick (Dick Jones) help an ex-convict (House Peters Jr.) who is accused of robbing a stage.
A beautiful girl and a jeweler steal gold-bearing stagecoaches.
An ex-convict makes a fresh start thanks to his son.
A quick-change artist's gang robs a wagon-carried mine payroll.
Range Rider (Jock Mahoney) and Dick (Dick Jones) come to the rescue of a millionaire (Erville Alderson) who has lost his memory and his daughter (Elaine Riley).
Range Rider and Dick become involved in a political battle when they save a woman and some ballot boxes.
A crooked cattle buyer collects antique dueling pistols.
Red frees himself from the noose and barely beats the outlaw's stagecoach across the finish line, winning the $5000 prize.
Red secures a confession from Grimes; Dade is trapped by Red and Cherokee in the act of destroying evidence.
Red and Cherokee escape from the burning jail; Red learns that the Ryder ranch is about to be foreclosed by Drake's agents.
Red barely escapes from the blast; in the aftermath of the explosion, he discovers papers linking Ace Hanlon to the raids on the ranchers.
A rancher organizes an opposition to a crooked banker.

Sheriff Lawson wires for a Federal Land Commissioner to check on the various titles to land in the Mesquite district; One-Eye, under orders from Drake, attempts to halt the stagecoach and kill Treadway, the land agent.

st: Murder on the Santa Fe Trail
d: Mesquite banker Calvin Drake plans to profit from Santa Fe Railroad by gaining control of all the land in the territory.
A young miner is kidnapped when it's learned that he's stumbled upon a bonanza.
A local miser is robbed by a con man hired to be his bodyguard.
An outlaw forces Roy to track down his missing horse.
Dale helps a falsely accused man escape from jail.
Doc Stevens' traveling store has a more sinister purpose.
The local postmaster plots to rob a train carrying a valuable bank shipment.
Dale and Roy must convince an 11-year-old boy help catch his outlaw brother.
A bank employee (Stanford Jolley) is forced to join a gang after being framed for embezzlement.
Roy, Dale and Pat help a wounded sheriff contain an outlaw gang in a desert oasis town.
A government agent poses as a minister's son to break up a gang of counterfeiters.
In the desert, three Old West outlaws (Chester Morris, Lewis Stone, Walter Brennan) adopt the baby of a dying woman.

t: If You Meet Sartana Pray for Your Death
d: Nobody knows a mysterious gunfighter who has joined a scramble for stagecoach gold.
(1967) A gang robs a gold shipment from a train. A so-called bounty hunter is sent to track down the robbers and decides to let them lead him to the gold.

t: Between God, the Devil and a Winchester
d: Violence and vultures follow when cowboys covet a special rifle.
A lawman (Guy Madison) finds his parents slain, his partner (Pietro Martellanza) held hostage and his town corrupt.
A gunslinger rescues his fiancée from the white slavers who abducted her.
Hoss befriends Charlie Trent, a man who went from top Army scout to town drunk after he led his troops into a massacre.
A Deputy U.S. Marshal arrives to escort a man to California to testify against a gang; guest Dan Duryea.

Silky inherits the Skookum Sentinel as payoff for a debt and finds that he is the latest victim of a reign of terror. Without help from anyone, he beats the gang at their own game and lures a willing lady to the side of law and order.

Pierre is accused of stealing $300,000 in gold dust when Rocky and the citizens of Yukon City are swayed by the oratory of an itinerant preacher. When his partner is killed, Pierre enlists the aid of a novice to help deliver the miners' gold.

Silky and his partner Harry hold a two-thirds interest in a gold mine with beautiful singer Fay, but for Silky it's a ticket to a lynching. When his partner disappears, Silky is accused of murder by John, the leading citizen of Argyll.

Pierre, delivering supplies to a doctor in a lonely Eskimo village, is betrayed by a jealous medicine man. When Pierre and Dr. Jim violate a tribal custom they incur the wrath of the medicine man and find themselves prisoners of two killers.

st: The Day of the Long Night
d: Jaimie and a friend stumble across a disturbed man (George Kennedy) and his sister in a foggy swamp.
Twelve-year-old Jaimie McPheeters, along with his father and a group of pioneers, travels westward from Paducah, Ky., to the California gold fields in 1849.

st: The Day of the Flying Dutchman
d: Doc meets a Dutchman, who is piloting a sail-driven wagon to California.
A former dance hall girl poses as a Spanish heiress to claim a land grant that includes part of the Ponderosa; guest Sebastian Cabot.
Jeb Drummond is a murderous sheep herder who has Adam taken hostage to try and force Ben to sign over a large section of Ponderosa land to him.
A Ponderosa ranch hand faces charges of killing the wife of the U.S. marshal who came to arrest him.
As Ben prepares to run for governor, Joe must come to his rescue when a disabled police officer from New Orleans comes to arrest Ben on a 20-year-old murder charge.
Adam is taken hostage by a band of U.S. Army prisoners who have escaped and sought refuge on the Ponderosa.
A wanderer seeking his parents' lynchers, arrives in Virginia City as Ben and Adam are convicted of murder.
An Oregon trapper (Tim McIntire) and his pregnant Apache mate (Serene Hedin) make their home on a Paiute burial ground.
A man (William Jordan) and a schoolmarm (Katherine Cannon) defend a lost Indian boy (Juan Gonzalez) and his stallion against town bigots circa 1900.
Two orphans (Heather Rattray, Mark Edward Hall) follow a frontier con man (Robert Logan) over the Rockies to their Oregon inheritance.
A cowboy proves to be a big hit with the ladies as he weaves his way through the Old West.
Rancher Joseph Colton buys cattle cars and intends to purchase the penniless line from principal stockholder Gwynn Randall.
A cowboy (John Wayne) romances a pretty woman (Marion Burns) while tracking the outlaw gang that killed his father.
A rodeo rider (John Wayne) and his assistant (Eddy Chandler) are accused of robbing and murdering a promoter and must assume new identities to track down and bring the real killers to justice.
Ben tries to help his paraplegic neighbor Tom by setting up a grain mill on his unused land; Tom's hired hand raises his suspicion about Ben's plan.
Outlaws plot to steal a trunk containing the savings of a religious group heading for a new life in the West.
A crook is mistakenly given cash designated for the construction of a clinic.
Two outlaws threaten to expose a bank teller with a criminal past.
Outlaws target the home of Don Jose while he is leading the annual Ride of the Ranchers.
Pat Brady buys an old ghost town inhabited by a strange old man (Tom London).
Dale helps investigate the mayor (Harry Lauter) of a small town who is suspected of being corrupt.
A young carnival worker is framed for the murder of his boss.
Pat Brady is elected sheriff just in time to catch a notorious killer.
Roy hires an ex-con who is quickly suspected of committing several recent robberies.
A woman from Connecticut arrives at Dale's café seeking her father.
A greedy veterinarian plans to murder a blind prospector who is using Roy's dog.
Roy and Pat aid a boxer (Charles Bronson) who has criminal connections.
Con men trick an unsuspecting Dale into selling the ranch.
A group of cattle rustlers tries to sell stolen beef to Dale's café.
The owner of a gun used to kill a rancher protests his innocence.
Roy and Dale discover the body of a murdered Indian chief.
The Mingo Kid swaps clothes with Roy, who is then taken hostage by another outlaw.
Quisto gets involved with the plight of a thieving orphaned boy; Collen aids a pregnant woman who's being pursued by border patrol.
A twelve-year-old is abducted in Los Angeles; clues found by the frantic Champion clan point to a procurer operating a child-prostitution ring.
A cattleman's association detective goes undercover as a ranch foreman to nab a gang of cattle rustlers.
Range detectives Johnny Bronton and Tucson Smith are out to trap and bring to justice a band of smugglers who have been bringing silver across the Mexican border illegally.
A federal agent tracks down a gang of counterfeiters operating along the Mexican border.
A federal agent poses as a prisoner in order to secure vital secrets from a fellow inmate concerning an outlaw gang.
Benton and the girl escape, and he forms a defensive barricade against the outlaws; Reade then figures he has to hold tight until the loan deadline.
Rich playboy Drogo Gaines is in imminent danger of marrying a gold digger; he escapes by feigning insanity.
Jim climbs from the water; apparently Wolf is killed; the outlaws retreat and find him half-drowned; he sends for every cutthroat in the region.
Jim Benton leads a group of vigilantes called the "Riders of Death Valley" that protect the local miners from the evil plans of Joseph Kirby and Rance Davis.
When Lucky spots Steve Langdon, a dead ringer for Collins, he arrests him.
In the split moment before the overtaking of the herd reaches him, Benton vaults to his saddle and safety, leaving Reade's men scattered and believing him dead.
A white man (Dennis Hopper) stands trial for killing a Mexican in 1848 California, just after the Mexican War.
A cattleman's association detective goes undercover as a ranch foreman to nab a gang of cattle rustlers.
A federal agent tracks down a gang of counterfeiters operating along the Mexican border.
A federal agent poses as a prisoner in order to secure vital secrets from a fellow inmate concerning an outlaw gang.
The Cartwrights' neighbor (Franchot Tone), a former soldier and lawman, seeks security for his daughter.
Bigoted Ike Daggett takes action when Ben gives an Indian and his wife land after the Indian saves his life.
After searching all night for the rustlers who attacked the saloon, Gordon returns to the Mulford ranch.
After climbing from the well into which he has crashed, Gordon returns to Mulford's ranch; Radigan, the foreman, learns that Gordon has sent for Pat Campbell.
Gordon and Campbell, galloping to rescue Mary from the burning wagon, are fired upon by the two rustlers; Campbell is mortally wounded.
After escaping the tunnel explosion, a raid on Mulford's cattle sends Gordon and Ed trailing the rustlers to Santa Rosa.
Gordon and Mary, fleeing from Santa Rosa, escape the cattle stampede, and elude the rustlers; Mary's grandfather has gone to Ghost City with Jed Wilson.
Gordon rescues Amos Gray from the burning house and sends him home in Wilson's buckboard; Mulford's cattle are rated again; Mulford sends Radigan for the sheriff.
As Gordon crosses the river, the rustlers open fire and sink from sight; coming up behind dense brush, he hears them refer to Radigan as their leader.
Spooky rescues Buck; Mary assures Hudson that Buck is trustworthy; Hudson reveals a secret to both of them.
Buck grabs Mary and leaps to safety in the mine tunnel, avoiding the explosion; Hudson returns from pursuing the renegade.
Buck rolls down an embankment and out of the path of the galloping horses; Buck rides off and the bandits head for Hudson's ranch after the gold.
Buck sees Roscoe in the nick of time; Roscoe is jailed; cowboys drive off his henchmen; Mary is thrown from her horse.
Outlaws terrorize ranchers near Maverick; Buck Grant, using the disguise of the Phantom Rider, battles against bandits.
Buck escapes death by rolling under a water trough a split second before the dynamite explosion; Spooky tells Buck a crooked deal is planned.
After numerous altercations with a white stallion, Roy comes to the conclusion he's got to get rid of it.
Chance is reunited with the mother he's never known; the Champions join hands to punish Jeb Hollister and restore justice.
Valley rustlers frame a G-man (Tim McCoy) who is posing as a Gypsy.
